title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Corinthians chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Corinthians Chapter 4.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Let a man so account of us
Moreover it is required in stewards
But with me it is a very small thing
For I know nothing by myself
questions.correctAnswer: Let a man so account of us
questions.explanation: This phrase appears first in the chapter, as stated in 1 Corinthians 4:1.

questions.question: What is required in stewards according to 1 Corinthians 4?
options: That a man be found faithful
That they know the mysteries of God
questions.correctAnswer: That a man be found faithful
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:2 states that it is required in stewards that a man be found faithful.

questions.question: Who does Paul say judges him?
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord
questions.explanation: According to 1 Corinthians 4:4, Paul states that he is not justified by himself but that he is judged by the Lord.

questions.question: What should we not do until the Lord comes?
questions.correctAnswer: Judge nothing before the time
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:5 instructs us to judge nothing before the time until the Lord comes.

questions.question: What will the Lord bring to light?
questions.correctAnswer: The hidden things of darkness
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:5 mentions that the Lord will bring to light the hidden things of darkness.

questions.question: To whom has Paul transferred these things?
questions.correctAnswer: To Apollos and himself
questions.explanation: According to 1 Corinthians 4:6, Paul has transferred these things to himself and Apollos for the sake of the brethren.

questions.question: What should we not think of men above?
questions.correctAnswer: What is written
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:6 advises not to think of men above that which is written.

questions.question: What question does Paul ask about differences among men?
options: Who maketh thee to differ from another?
questions.correctAnswer: Who maketh thee to differ from another?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:7 poses the question, 'For who maketh thee to differ from another?'.

questions.question: What does Paul imply about what one has received?
options: It should not be boasted about
questions.correctAnswer: It should not be boasted about
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 4:7, Paul indicates that if one has received something, they should not glory as if they had not received it.

questions.question: Is it important for stewards to be found faithful?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:2 clearly states that it is required in stewards that a man be found faithful.

questions.question: According to Paul, should he judge his own self?
questions.correctAnswer: No
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:3 states that Paul judges not his own self.

questions.question: True or False: Paul states that he knows nothing by himself.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:4 states, 'For I know nothing by myself'.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will judge hidden things.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:5 indicates that the Lord will bring to light hidden things.

questions.question: True or False: Paul says that glorying in what one has received is encouraged.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:7 suggests that one should not glory as if they had not received what they have.

questions.question: True or False: Paul advises to judge others before the Lord comes.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:5 instructs not to judge anything before the time until the Lord comes.

medium.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Corinthians Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 4:8, what does Paul say the Corinthians are now?
options: Full, rich, and reigning as kings without us
Faithful stewards of the mysteries of God
Despised and defamed by the world
questions.correctAnswer: Full, rich, and reigning as kings without us
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:8 states, 'Now ye are full, now ye are rich, ye have reigned as kings without us.'

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 4:9 say will happen as a result of God setting forth the apostles last?
options: They are made a spectacle unto the world, angels, and men
They will be full and rich
They will be honored by all
questions.correctAnswer: They are made a spectacle unto the world, angels, and men
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:9 says God has appointed the apostles to death and made them a spectacle unto the world, angels, and men, as a consequence of being set forth last.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 4:10, how does Paul contrast the apostles with the Corinthians?
options: We are fools for Christ's sake, but ye are wise in Christ
We are rich, but ye are poor
We are reigning, but ye are servants
We are honored, but ye are despised
questions.correctAnswer: We are fools for Christ's sake, but ye are wise in Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:10 contrasts the apostles being fools for Christ's sake while the Corinthians are wise in Christ.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 4:12-13, what is the relationship between being reviled or persecuted and how the apostles respond?
options: Being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it
Being reviled, we curse; being persecuted, we retaliate
Being reviled, we ignore; being persecuted, we flee
Being reviled, we rejoice; being persecuted, we judge
questions.correctAnswer: Being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it
questions.explanation: Verses 12 and 13 state that when reviled, the apostles bless, and when persecuted, they endure it, showing their patient endurance.

questions.question: What does Paul say about the apostles’ physical conditions in 1 Corinthians 4:11?
options: They hunger, thirst, are naked, buffeted, and have no certain dwelling place
They are wealthy and well housed
They travel in comfort and honor
They feast daily and wear fine clothes
questions.correctAnswer: They hunger, thirst, are naked, buffeted, and have no certain dwelling place
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:11 describes the apostles’ hardships: hunger, thirst, nakedness, buffeting, and homelessness.

questions.question: How does Paul describe the apostles in 1 Corinthians 4:13?
options: As the filth of the world and the offscouring of all things
questions.correctAnswer: As the filth of the world and the offscouring of all things
questions.explanation: Verse 13 says the apostles are made as the filth of the world and the offscouring of all things unto this day.

questions.question: What reason does Paul give in 1 Corinthians 4:14 for writing these things to the Corinthians?
options: I write not to shame you, but as my beloved sons I warn you
I write to rebuke and punish you
I write to boast about my sufferings
questions.correctAnswer: I write not to shame you, but as my beloved sons I warn you
questions.explanation: In verse 14, Paul clarifies he writes as a loving father warning his beloved sons, not to shame them.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 4:12 illustrate the apostles’ attitude toward labor and persecution?
options: Labouring with their own hands, reviled they bless; persecuted they suffer
They complain about labor and persecution
questions.correctAnswer: Labouring with their own hands, reviled they bless; persecuted they suffer
questions.explanation: Verse 12 highlights the apostles’ perseverance and grace in labor and persecution, blessing when reviled and suffering when persecuted.

questions.question: What does Paul imply about the Corinthians’ attitude in 1 Corinthians 4:8 compared to the apostles’ reality in verses 9-13?
options: The Corinthians are proud and self-sufficient while apostles suffer
The Corinthians are humble and suffering
The apostles are rich and reigning
The apostles are ignoring the Corinthians
questions.correctAnswer: The Corinthians are proud and self-sufficient while apostles suffer
questions.explanation: Verse 8 shows the Corinthians acting as if they are full and reigning, contrasting with apostles’ sufferings in following verses.

questions.question: What spiritual lesson can be drawn from the apostles being 'made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men' in 1 Corinthians 4:9?
options: Faithfulness may lead to public suffering but is witnessed in heaven and earth
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness may lead to public suffering but is witnessed in heaven and earth
questions.explanation: Verse 9 indicates apostles suffer publicly yet their faithfulness is observed by both heavenly and earthly beings.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 4:10, how are the apostles described in terms of strength and honor compared to the Corinthians?
options: We are weak but strong; we are honorable but despised
We are strong and honored; you are weak and despised
We are wise and rich; you are fools and poor
We are kings; you are servants
questions.correctAnswer: We are weak but strong; we are honorable but despised
questions.explanation: Verse 10 contrasts the apostles’ weakness and despising with their true strength and honor in Christ.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'working with our own hands' in 1 Corinthians 4:12 suggest about the apostles’ approach to labor?
options: They support themselves and do not rely on others
They avoid work and depend on others
questions.correctAnswer: They support themselves and do not rely on others
questions.explanation: Verse 12 shows apostles laboring with their own hands, indicating self-support and diligent work.

questions.question: What does Paul urge the Corinthians not to do in 1 Corinthians 4:6?
options: Not to think of men above that which is written
Not to work with their own hands
Not to be reviled or persecuted
questions.correctAnswer: Not to think of men above that which is written
questions.explanation: Verse 6 advises the Corinthians to avoid pride and judging others beyond Scripture’s teaching.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 4:14 states Paul writes to shame the Corinthians for their behavior.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 14 clearly says Paul does not write to shame them but to warn them as beloved sons.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 4:2, it is required that a steward be found faithful.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:2 states that it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.

hard.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Corinthians Chapter 4.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 4:15, who has begotten the Corinthians through the gospel?
questions.correctAnswer: Paul
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Paul, as stated in 1 Corinthians 4:15: 'for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel.'

questions.question: What does Paul beseech the Corinthians to do in 1 Corinthians 4:16?
questions.correctAnswer: Be followers of him
questions.explanation: Paul asks the Corinthians to be followers of him in 1 Corinthians 4:16: 'Wherefore I beseech you, be ye followers of me.'

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 4:17, who does Paul send to the Corinthians to remind them of his ways?
questions.correctAnswer: Timotheus
questions.explanation: Paul sends Timotheus to remind the Corinthians of his ways in 1 Corinthians 4:17: 'For this cause have I sent unto you Timotheus.'

questions.question: What does Paul imply about the kingdom of God in 1 Corinthians 4:20?
questions.correctAnswer: It is in power
questions.explanation: Paul states in 1 Corinthians 4:20 that 'For the kingdom of God is not in word, but in power.'

questions.question: What does Paul express he will do shortly if the Lord wills, according to 1 Corinthians 4:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Know their speech
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 4:19, Paul indicates he will know 'not the speech of them which are puffed up, but the power.'

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 4:21, how does Paul ask the Corinthians if he should come to them?
options: With a rod or in love
questions.correctAnswer: With a rod or in love
questions.explanation: Paul asks, 'What will ye? shall I come unto you with a rod, or in love, and in the spirit of meekness?' in 1 Corinthians 4:21.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'begotten' in 1 Corinthians 4:15 imply about Paul's relationship to the Corinthians?
questions.correctAnswer: To become a father
questions.explanation: The Greek word implies a paternal relationship, as Paul sees himself as a spiritual father to the Corinthians.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in 1 Corinthians 4:19 when Paul contrasts speech and power?
questions.correctAnswer: Antithesis
questions.explanation: Antithesis is used to contrast the idea of 'speech' and 'power' in 1 Corinthians 4:19.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the idea of spiritual fatherhood mentioned in 1 Corinthians 4:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Galatians 4:19
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:19 echoes the theme of spiritual fatherhood, as Paul refers to the Galatians as his children in Christ.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of following Christ's example as indicated in 1 Corinthians 4:16?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Peter 2:21
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:21 fulfills the theme of following Christ's example, as it encourages believers to walk in His footsteps.

questions.question: What comes before 1 Corinthians 4:15?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 4:14
questions.explanation: The verse preceding 1 Corinthians 4:15 is 1 Corinthians 4:14, where Paul refers to the Corinthians as beloved sons.

questions.question: According to the context of 1 Corinthians 4:7, what must one remember about their gifts?
questions.correctAnswer: They are received
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:7 emphasizes that all gifts are received, not earned, as it states, 'what hast thou that thou didst not receive?'.

questions.question: In the context of 1 Corinthians 4, Paul uses the term 'puffed up' to describe what attitude?
questions.correctAnswer: Pride
questions.explanation: The term 'puffed up' in 1 Corinthians 4:18 refers to an attitude of pride among some Corinthians.

questions.question: True or False: Paul instructs the Corinthians to disregard their spiritual fathers.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: False, as Paul emphasizes his role as a spiritual father in 1 Corinthians 4:15.

questions.question: True or False: The kingdom of God is described by Paul as being in power rather than mere words.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: True, as stated in 1 Corinthians 4:20, where Paul declares that 'the kingdom of God is not in word, but in power.'

theological.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Corinthians Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 4:2 teach about stewardship and faithfulness in the Christian life?
options: Faithfulness is a required quality in stewards of God's mysteries
Stewards are only accountable to human judgment
Faithfulness is optional for ministers of Christ
Stewardship guarantees salvation regardless of faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness is a required quality in stewards of God's mysteries
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:2 states that it is required that a man be found faithful as a steward, emphasizing the doctrine that faithfulness is essential in managing God's mysteries.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is taught in 1 Corinthians 4:4 regarding self-assessment and God's judgment?
options: Only the Lord can justly judge a believer, not human beings
Believers should rely primarily on their own judgment
Human judgment is superior to divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Only the Lord can justly judge a believer, not human beings
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:4 explains that Paul does not judge himself and is not justified by his own knowledge; rather, the one who judges him is the Lord, teaching the doctrine that divine judgment alone is ultimate and just.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 4:7 teach about human ability and grace in regard to spiritual gifts?
options: All spiritual gifts and distinctions are received from God, not by human merit
Spiritual gifts are earned by human effort
Differences among believers come from natural talent
Glorying in gifts is justified because they are self-produced
questions.correctAnswer: All spiritual gifts and distinctions are received from God, not by human merit
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:7 emphasizes that no one has anything they did not receive, and therefore boasting as if one had not received is misplaced, teaching the doctrine of grace as the source of all spiritual gifts.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 4:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:5 teaches that the Lord will bring to light hidden things and make manifest the counsels of the hearts, demonstrating God's omniscience—His all-knowing nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 1 Corinthians 4:9 concerning the apostles' sufferings as a testimony to the world and angels?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:9 describes how God appointed the apostles as a spectacle to the world, angels, and men, demonstrating His sovereignty in orchestrating salvation history and His authoritative control over their sufferings.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 4:14–15 connect to the broader biblical theme of spiritual fatherhood and gospel ministry?
options: It parallels Paul’s role as a spiritual father who begets believers through the gospel, reflecting themes in Acts and pastoral epistles
It contradicts the idea of multiple instructors by promoting isolation
It denies the importance of gospel proclamation in spiritual birth
It asserts that physical parentage is superior to spiritual
questions.correctAnswer: It parallels Paul’s role as a spiritual father who begets believers through the gospel, reflecting themes in Acts and pastoral epistles
questions.explanation: Verses 14–15 show Paul warning and calling the Corinthians his beloved sons, having begotten them in Christ through the gospel, which fits with New Testament themes of spiritual fatherhood seen elsewhere in Acts and pastoral letters.

questions.question: What is the redemptive-historical significance of 1 Corinthians 4:20’s teaching that 'the kingdom of God is not in word, but in power'?
options: It emphasizes the inaugurated eschatology where God's kingdom is present in power through the Spirit, not just proclaimed verbally
It teaches that words alone are sufficient for kingdom realization
It denies the present activity of the Spirit in the church
It suggests that the kingdom is a future event only with no present effect
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the inaugurated eschatology where God's kingdom is present in power through the Spirit, not just proclaimed verbally
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:20 teaches the kingdom of God is realized in power, reflecting the New Testament doctrine that the kingdom is inaugurated in Christ’s resurrection and Spirit-empowered church, not merely proclaimed in words.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 4:1 and 4:2 teach about Christian ministry and stewardship?
options: Ministers of Christ are stewards of God's mysteries and must be found faithful in their stewardship
Ministers are autonomous and need not be accountable
Stewardship is unrelated to faithfulness in ministry
Human judgment is the final authority in evaluating ministers
questions.correctAnswer: Ministers of Christ are stewards of God's mysteries and must be found faithful in their stewardship
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:1 calls ministers stewards of the mysteries of God, and 4:2 emphasizes that faithfulness is required in stewards, teaching the integrated doctrine of faithful stewardship in Christian ministry.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 4:10 and 4:11 teach about the paradox of apostolic weakness and suffering in relation to Christ's wisdom and strength?
options: Apostles are weak and despised in the world yet embody Christ’s wisdom and strength through suffering
Apostles are honored by the world and free from suffering
Weakness disqualifies apostles from representing Christ
Christ’s wisdom is independent of suffering and weakness
questions.correctAnswer: Apostles are weak and despised in the world yet embody Christ’s wisdom and strength through suffering
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:10 contrasts the apostles’ foolishness and weakness with the Corinthians’ wisdom and strength, while 4:11 lists their sufferings, teaching the doctrine of apostolic paradox where weakness and suffering reveal Christ’s power.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 4:18 and 4:19 teach about Paul's authority and the nature of his forthcoming visit?
options: Paul will come with the power of the Spirit, not merely words, addressing the arrogance of some
Paul will avoid confrontation and only use gentle words
Paul denies any authority over the church
Paul’s visit will have no spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: Paul will come with the power of the Spirit, not merely words, addressing the arrogance of some
questions.explanation: Verses 18 and 19 reveal some are arrogant, but Paul asserts he will come in power and not be impressed by mere speech, affirming his Spirit-empowered authority to correct pride.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 1 Corinthians 4:14-17 shows Paul’s ministry is authoritarian and harsh. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Paul lovingly warns as a spiritual father and sends Timothy to remind them of his gentle ways
Paul commands without regard for the Corinthians’ wellbeing
Paul rejects all forms of correction to avoid conflict
Paul’s ministry is solely punitive and lacks pastoral care
questions.correctAnswer: Paul lovingly warns as a spiritual father and sends Timothy to remind them of his gentle ways
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:14-17 shows Paul writes to warn as a beloved father and sends Timothy, a faithful son, to remind the church of Paul's manner in Christ, demonstrating pastoral care rather than authoritarianism.

questions.question: What doctrine about human pride and divine grace is taught in 1 Corinthians 4:6?
options: Believers must not think of anyone beyond what is written to avoid pride and rivalry
It encourages self-exaltation based on human wisdom
It promotes elevating church leaders above scripture
It denies the authority of scripture in community relationships
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must not think of anyone beyond what is written to avoid pride and rivalry
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:6 uses Paul and Apollos as examples to instruct believers not to think beyond what is written, preventing pride and division, teaching doctrinal humility and scriptural authority.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is illustrated by the Lord’s role as judge in 1 Corinthians 4:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:4 affirms that the Lord is the one who judges Paul, showing God’s attribute of perfect justice as the righteous judge of hearts.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of the apostles being described as 'fools for Christ’s sake' and 'the offscouring of all things' in 1 Corinthians 4:10-13?
options: Their suffering and low status reveal the paradox of the cross and the power of God in weakness
They are ineffective leaders rejected by God
Their humiliation indicates a lack of divine approval
Their status is irrelevant to the gospel message
questions.correctAnswer: Their suffering and low status reveal the paradox of the cross and the power of God in weakness
questions.explanation: Verses 10-13 describe apostles’ humiliation as part of their witness, teaching the doctrine that God’s power is made perfect in human weakness, reflecting the paradox of the cross.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 4:21 link the theme of church discipline with Christlike character?
options: It presents discipline as either loving correction or severity, both exercised in meekness
It rejects the use of any corrective discipline
It separates discipline from spiritual character
questions.correctAnswer: It presents discipline as either loving correction or severity, both exercised in meekness
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:21 poses the question whether Paul will come with a rod or in love and meekness, teaching that church discipline should reflect Christlike humility and love.
